attributes.text: Both ends are AI agents who can work out what's needed and ask each other. Code that decided for them only added parts to break. So the mailbox just stores, routers just nudge, and agents do the judging. File safety stays in code, because agents can't reason their way around a corrupted file.

All 15 checks pass after the cut, including the new ones for finding new mail and waiting for it. The command still reads the real mailbox, older records included.
The mail command is about a fifth smaller. It keeps safe storage, channels, catch-up, send, reply and per-person marks, and adds two small commands so routers can spot new mail.
The router instructions are rewritten. It now only tells sessions they have mail, with no records and no lock on being the router. Not yet run live.
The session instructions are shorter. Sessions read their own inbox, judge what's theirs, and ask the other agent when unsure. Not yet installed.
The simpler agreement needs Codex to look at it and Al to accept it. Codex has been told. Nothing on Codex's side is built against the old version, so nothing breaks.
